Jubilant Ingrevia Limited 
Q2 & H1 FY27 Earnings Conference Call Transcript 
October 27, 2026 
 
Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Jubilant Ingrevia's Q2 and H1 
FY27 Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the 
listen-only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the 
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, 
please signal an operator by pressing star then zero on your touchtone phone. 
Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over 
to Mr. Pavleen Taneja, Head of Investor Relations at Jubilant Ingrevia Limited. Thank 
you and over to you, sir. 
Pavleen Taneja: 
Thank you, Iqra. Good evening, everyone. Thank you for joining the Q2 FY2027 
Earnings Conference Call of Jubilant Ingrevia Limited. I would like to remind you that 
some of some of the statements made on the call today could be forward-looking in 
nature and a detailed disclaimer in this regard has been included in the press release 
and the result presentation that has been shared on our website. On the call today, 
we have Mr. Shyam Bhartia, Chairman, Mr. Hari Bhartia, Co-Chairman, Mr. Deepak 
Jain, CEO and Managing Director and Mr. Varun Gupta, CFO, Jubilant Ingrevia 
Limited. I now invite Mr. Shyam Bhartia to share his comments. 
Shyam Bhartia: 
Thank you, Pavleen. Very good evening to all of you. We are pleased to report that 
we continued to sustain strong growth momentum in Q2 with revenue growing 24% 
year-on-year and EBITDA increasing 51%, reflecting disciplined execution across our 
businesses. Our quarterly EBITDA has more than doubled over the past 3 years, 
underscoring the successful execution of our pinnacle strategy and continued focus 
on disciplined cost management.  
This momentum was also reflected in our strong first half performance with revenue 
growing 25% and EBITDA by 44% year-on-year. We are also delighted to announce 
that we have signed an agreement to acquire 40% stake in Zettaone Technologies 
Limited. This marks our entry into electronics design management system space 
which will enable us to offer more integrated value proposition to customers in the 
electronics and semiconductor sectors.  
Now let me take you through the key developments across the market we operate in.  
Acetyls 
Amid continued geopolitical uncertainties, volumes remain stable while pharma crude 
prices supported improved realization. However, input and utility costs during the 
quarter partially offset the benefits of improved pricing. 
Pharmaceuticals 

 
Page 3 of 12 
 
The pharmaceutical segment continues to grow supported by steady volumes and 
sustained demand for intermediates.  
Agro-chemicals 
The agro-chemical segment remained under pressure with stable volumes but muted 
pricing, primarily due to excess capacity in China.  
Personal care  
We continued to witness strong volume growth in personal care alongside increasing 
traction with new customers seeking outsourcing partnerships.  
Nutrition 
The nutrition segment maintained steady volumes despite some softening in vitamin 
B3 pricing in the animal feed segment over the past few weeks. Semiconductors and 
electronics. We continue to see strong growth in our new molecule pipeline with 
encouraging customer traction, particularly in Japan. This reinforces our confidence 
in the growth opportunities emerging in these sectors.  
Now let me share few details of our future outlook. Our pinnacle journey continues to 
progress well, supported by strong revenue and EBITDA growth, along with robust 
pipeline of growth opportunities. We remain confident of sustaining this momentum 
with growth expected across all three business segments in FY2027.  
Within Acetyls in particular, we anticipate higher volumes supported by planned 
closures in Europe. Additionally, our new multipurpose plant remains on track for 
commissioning by the year-end. This will further strengthen our CDMO and fine 
chemicals growth roadmap and enhance our ability to capitalize on emerging 
opportunities. With this, I hand over to Deepak for detailed business overview. 
Deepak Jain: 
Thank you very much, Mr. Bhartia, and a very good evening to all of you. We 
appreciate your participation in our Q2 and H1 FY27 investor call. Let me start by 
giving a quick overview of our business. We continued to execute well against our 
strategic priorities despite ongoing global uncertainties. 
Our diversified sourcing capabilities, strong customer partnerships, and agile 
operations enabled us to effectively navigate these disruptions and price volatility 
while managing cost pass-throughs. This execution strength is clearly reflected in our 
performance during Q2 and H1 FY27. We delivered another strong quarter in Q2, 
reinforcing our performance for H1 FY27. 
Revenue reached an all-time high of INR1,394 crore, up 24% year-on-year, 
supported by stronger realizations and stable volumes. EBITDA rose 51% year-on-
year to INR 221 crore, the highest in the last three years, while PAT increased 60% 
year-on-year to INR111 crore. In specialty chemicals, the business delivered a strong 
performance with revenue reaching INR560 crore, up 16% year-on-year and 5% 
sequentially, led by healthy volume growth across fine chemicals and CDMO. 
We delivered EBITDA of INR140 crore, translating into a strong EBITDA margin of 
25%, driven by improved pricing across our value-added fine chemicals and CDMO 
portfolio. In pyridine and picolines, volumes remained stable despite continued 

 
Page 4 of 12 
 
softness in pricing. Our ongoing cost optimization and capacity debottlenecking 
initiatives are expected to strengthen performance going forward. 
Our fine chemicals business delivered broad-based growth across pyridine and 
diketene derivatives, supported by improved pricing with particularly strong 
momentum in the diketene portfolio. In personal care, we have multiple products 
under development and are seeing increasing traction across key personal care 
segments and customers. 
Our CDMO business continued to build strong momentum across agro, pharma, 
personal care, and semiconductors. Agro delivered healthy volume growth led by 
higher innovator CDMO volumes, while we are seeing strong customer engagement 
in pharma with our US and Europe roadshows with innovators.  
In semiconductors, we continue to see growing inquiries and an expanding 
application pipeline, supported by our upcoming R&D and cleanroom facility in 
Greater Noida. Overall, we have 25 plus confirmed molecules in our pipeline, which 
are expected to drive our future growth in coming years. In nutrition and health 
solution business, it delivered another stronger quarter with revenue reaching 
INR270 crore, up 50% year-on-year and 11% sequentially.  
EBITDA increased to INR39 crore, representing growth of 87% year-on-year and 9% 
sequentially, while margins remained healthy at 15%. Within human nutrition, B3 
delivered strong volume growth, both year-on-year and sequentially, led by double-
digit growth across food and cosmetic applications. CCCBT also witnessed improved 
volumes and pricing, supported by strong customer traction across EU, US, and 
India.  
In premixes, the Remidex integration continues to strengthen engagement and sales 
with tier-1 customers in India. Our animal nutrition business also continued to show 
healthy momentum. B3 delivered strong double-digit volume growth both year-on-
year and sequentially, while pricing remained marginally soft. Choline maintained its 
domestic market position with continued traction and sequential improvement in 
volumes in Europe. 
Premixes also delivered strong pricing improvement supporting healthy margin 
performance. In chemical intermediates business, it delivered another strong quarter 
with steady volumes and improved realizations amid higher input costs arising from 
elevated crude prices. Segment revenue grew 24% year-on-year and 8% 
sequentially to INR563 crore. 
EBITDA rose significantly to INR64 crore, up 26% year-on-year and 13% 
sequentially, driven by improved realizations across the product portfolio. Acetic 
anhydride delivered healthy sequential volume growth supported by resilient pharma 
demand and market share gains in Europe while maintaining a stable domestic 
market position.  
We also witnessed a strong double-digit pricing improvement year-on-year and with 
the competitor plants closure in Europe, we expect a further strengthening of demand 
and pricing going forward. Ethyl acetate continued to see steady sequential volume 
growth while realizations improved significantly both year-on-year and quarter-on-
quarter, reflecting the elevated input cost environment.  

 
Page 5 of 12 
 
Let me also share the update on M&A, specifically on Zettaone. I am delighted to 
share that we have recently signed an agreement to acquire 40% stake in Zettaone 
with an investment of INR189 crore.  
The transaction is progressing well and the shareholders agreement will also be 
concluded soon. Zettaone operates in the electronics design and manufacturing 
services space, providing us access to the broader electronics and semiconductor 
ecosystem. This transaction will enable us to deliver an integrated value proposition 
in electronics and semiconductor space, leading to long-term and sustainable value 
creation. 
We are already witnessing encouraging customer traction with several discussions 
underway with mid-sized and large customers. Zettaone will also broaden our access 
to new customers and deepen relationships with OEMs and technology companies 
across semiconductors, aerospace, defense, industrial, and related electronics 
segment. Zettaone has delivered a strong growth over the last three years and based 
on the current momentum, we expect the business to grow by at least 60% to 70% 
this year. 
The company is also establishing a new manufacturing facility in near Bangalore, 
which will further support its growth journey. With the strong momentum achieved in 
the first half of FY27, we are increasingly confident that our pinnacle strategy is 
delivering the desired outcomes. We believe FY27 will be a pivotal year in our 
journey, providing a strong foundation to accelerate growth and create greater value 
in the quarters ahead. We will now be happy to address any questions that you may 
have. Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you very much, sir. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. 
Anyone who wishes to ask a question, they press star and one on their touchtone 
telephone. If you wish to remove yourself from the question queue, you may press 
star and two. Participants are requested to use headsets while asking a question. 
Ladies and gentlemen, we will wait for a moment while the question queue 
assembles. The first question is from the line of Siddharth Gadekar from Equirus 
Securities. Please go ahead. 
Siddharth Gadekar: Good evening. 
Deepak Jain: 
Hi Siddharth. 
Siddharth Gadekar: So the first question is on our annual guidance of INR750 crore, 800 crore. Now, 
given that this European closure has come in somewhere in mid-September and also 
our guidance did not include any contribution on the large CDMO contract in the 
second half. So, how should we think about the guidance now for the full year? 
Deepak Jain: 
Thank you, Siddharth. Good question. I think we are sticking to our guidance. In fact, 
we think we should given the strong performance in the first half of the year, we 
should hopefully be closer to the upper end of the guidance we have given for the 
year. Regarding your question on the plant closure in Europe, it is a very recent 
development and things are still playing out on the ground. So, we expect some uplift 
starting to happen only from early part of next calendar year. How much of that can 
be captured in this year we will have to see, but we will look at it as a as a multi-year 
opportunity of course and hope to get a big blip in FY28 from that opportunity. 

 
Page 6 of 12 
 
Siddharth Gadekar: Got it. The second is now on the large CDMO contract. So now how should one think 
about this given that have we got any further visibility on the orders or any take-or-
pay commitment? 
Deepak Jain: 
So, as I have communicated in the past, the first lot that we received as an order 
from the customer that has been delivered in fact now as per the commitment and 
understanding with the customer. For future volumes, as I said in the past, there 
have been several scenarios which we have discussed with the customer. We are 
very close to concluding what the way forward would be and as soon as we have the 
visibility, we will be able to disclose that to all of you, hopefully within next few weeks. 
Siddharth Gadekar: And this is the last question is in this quarter, we have seen a very significant jump in 
the consumer segment. What has driven that growth and is this something that can 
continue and what is driving this growth? 
Deepak Jain: 
Yes, that is a good observation. I am glad you observed it. I think one of the big 
reasons is as I think I have communicated in the past, we have been focusing in a 
big way on the personal care segment and while we already have vitamin B3 
personal grade which has ramped up very quickly in recent months, we also have a 
few other products and a CDMO kind of opportunities where we have started to serve 
the customers. So, all of that has started to show a noticeable difference, but it is still 
at only 7% of our overall portfolio. We are hoping that this slice in our overall pie 
chart will increase much faster going forward and will hopefully reach double digits 
within next few quarters. 
Siddharth Gadekar: Is this entirely vitamin B3 the human grade contribution or there is something else 
also driving this? 
Deepak Jain: 
Like I said, there are other projects also. They may not have a very meaningful 
contribution right now, but as they scale up, it will start to contribute strongly in the 
overall contribution of consumer segment in the portfolio. 
Siddharth Gadekar: Okay, thank you. Thank you so much. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Abhijit Akella from Kotak Institutional 
Equities. Please go ahead. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Good evening. Thank you so much for taking my questions. First one was just on this 
Europe closure. Would appreciate your thoughts on just how large an opportunity this 
opens up for us. You know, any numbers in terms of market potential and things like 
that would be helpful. 
Deepak Jain: 
Yes, Abhijit, we are still getting a good grasp on what the quantum of opportunity 
could be. But as we have said in the past, we have significant share in Europe 
already in acetic anhydride, let us say high teens close to 20%. Our aspiration has 
been to double our market share. We feel on the back of this opportunity over the 
course of next couple of years, we should be able to do that. Provided the plants 
remain shut, which in itself right now the concerned company has to provide more 
visibility into. So, we are we are assessing all possible scenarios, but it would be a 
meaningfully large opportunity if it materializes. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Understood. Thank you. And the other one was just on you know, how much 
excluding the large agrochemical contract, how much revenue from the rest of the 

 
Page 7 of 12 
 
order book are we expecting to book in our P&L this year and next year? If it is 
possible to share some insight around that? 
Deepak Jain: 
Yes, I think that is a good question again and I know a lot of you have asked that 
question. So, in the previous few quarters, we announced that we have 25 plus 
opportunities which we have secured commercial orders to with a peak potential 
revenue of INR1,500 crore plus.  
On the back of some of the incremental opportunities that we have secured, that full 
potential along with the big contract is close to INR2,000 crore, but even if I keep the 
big contract aside, we still have a big pipeline which I mentioned in my opening 
remarks also, with the peak potential of almost INR1,500 crore plus and at least one 
third of that we will we will clock in in in this year, in this fiscal year itself, and we are 
hoping that not only that will scale up in coming years in quarters and years, but also 
will keep adding more to it because our larger funnel is much bigger than what we 
have already secured.  
So, stepping back and I think this thing, this one thing we have discussed Abhijit with 
you but also with others also, our CDMO story is much bigger and wider than just 
one contract, where also we will provide the visibility as I mentioned to Siddharth in 
response to his question, but the overall momentum across the broader set of 
opportunities we have is very high and on the back of that funnel, in last two years, 
even without including the revenue of the bigger contract this year in first two 
quarters, our revenues have almost doubled within last two years. So, that is the kind 
of momentum we are seeing and from here it is only going to accelerate and become 
larger because the base has also become larger. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Yes, the question I had was one was on the Zettaone opportunity if you could just 
share your thoughts regarding what the trajectory could be over the next two, three 
years and whether we are planning to account for it as an associate on the P&L. The 
other one was just on the capex. We have done about INR120 odd crore in the first 
half. What should the full year number look like? 
Deepak Jain: 
Yes, on the on Zettaone first it is a very strategic partnership for us. As I mentioned in 
my opening remarks, we see a huge value creation opportunity here given how fast 
that's that space is growing for India in the electronics manufacturing and design 
space. The market is growing at 35%, 40% every year. So on the standalone basis 
itself we feel the company should grow very fast and I think we have disclosed some 
of the numbers when we disclosed our partnership publicly a few weeks back. 
In the last few years, the business has doubled and even this year, we are hoping it 
will grow at least 60% 70% and possibly even more. So, the idea is to maintain that 
kind of growth over the next few years and even accelerate from here on the back of 
this partnership. There are a couple of elements of synergy here.  
Number one is as I as we have been saying, it helps us offer an integrated value 
proposition in semiconductor and electronics space. They have access to customers, 
they have credibility with the customers, they understand what those customers need 
and they themselves also use some of the electronic chemicals.  
So, all of that helps us in building huge credibility and rapport with the customers as 
we are having those conversations and that has already started to happen because 
our semiconductor funnel has already increased by almost 30% in last few months 

 
Page 8 of 12 
 
itself on the back of all the efforts we are doing jointly with them on the go-to-market 
side. 
At the same time, they have a need to scale up their manufacturing in a big way and 
which is where Jubilant comes in because we are operationally strong, we run big 
plants, complex plants and we are helping them scale up manufacturing quickly so 
that they can serve all the traction and orders that they are expecting to get from their 
customers. So, on the back of both these things, we feel it is a very synergistic 
partnership which will not only help scale Zettaone by an order of magnitude in 
coming years, but at the same time it will also accelerate the growth of our 
electronics and semiconductor chemicals. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Thank you. Just on the capex question, please, if it is possible? 
Deepak Jain: 
Yes, on the capex front, Abhijit, we maintain what we have said. We will be investing 
at least INR400 crore to INR500 crore every year as we announced a couple of years 
back in our investor presentation also. On an average, we are creating two new 
plants, ideally multipurpose plants every year. The Gajraula multipurpose plant will 
be ready in in next few months itself and we are in the process of conceptualizing 
couple of other investments. 
So, on the back of that, on a multi-year average perspective, I think every year we 
will be investing at least INR400 crore, INR500 crore to support, because the pipeline 
that we have ahead of us will require more facilities, more multipurpose plants. So, 
we are already in the process of doing that and as and when we get the approval 
from our board on the same, we will come back and make specific announcements 
on those specific capex that we have planned. 
Abhijit Akella: 
Thank you so much. All the best. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Nitesh Dhoot from Anand Rathi 
Institutional Equities. Please go ahead. 
Nitesh Dhoot: 
Good evening, team. My first question is on the Specialty Chemicals segment. So for 
H1, you know, we have grown our revenues at 14% and 9% EBITDA growth year-on-
year. So any indications we can give for the growth numbers, both revenue and 
EBITDA for Specialty Chemicals segment, particularly for H2 and for the next year? 
And how much of that growth in absolute numbers are we targeting from CDMO? 
Deepak Jain: 
Yes, the, the specialty chemical business, as you can imagine, and especially when 
the share of CDMO kind of, products and projects is increasing in them, it is always 
slightly lumpy in nature. As and when we start serving some of the big orders, it 
shows a kicker and, and step change in the trajectory, and in some quarters it may 
be even lower, like we have seen in couple of quarters back as well. 
But at an overall level, our aspiration is to continue to grow our specialty chemical 
portfolio at 20% to 25% year on year on a multi-year CAGR basis. Now that does not 
necessarily mean every quarter we will see 20%, 25%. If you take the last three 
years growth trajectory of our specialty chemical, it has, it has shown that kind of 
growth rate on EBITDA terms because we have optimized the business a lot. 
And we are sitting on a higher base of our legacy products as well. But as, as I 
mentioned earlier in response to Abhijit's question, as our, CDMO portfolio, where, 

 
Page 9 of 12 
 
like I said, of the full potential, one-third we are getting this year, as it starts kicking in, 
hopefully starting next year itself, we will see a steady growth trajectory there as well. 
Nitesh Dhoot: 
Sure. Thank you. And the next one is on the, on the Innovator, you know. So 
basically, the Innovator converted its revolving credit facility to secured, a few months 
back, you know, with subsidiary guarantees and asset pledges. So how is your take-
or-pay receivable protected there? I mean, is there a parent guarantee or a letter of 
credit or, or any, any other buffer? Or any colour that you can give there? 
Deepak Jain: 
Yes, I will not be able to comment on what they are doing, but as I have maintained 
in the past, we have a very solid agreement as well as understanding with them. Our 
risk is fully protected as per that arrangement, and with all the discussions we have 
done, we are very close to finalizing what will -- what future will look like. So right now 
I cannot provide that visibility, but hopefully within a few weeks we will come back 
and let you know. 
Nitesh Dhoot: 
All right. Thank you so much and wish you all the best for the coming quarters. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Harsh Shah. Please go ahead. 
Harsh Shah: 
Yes, thank you for giving me the opportunity. You have just now mentioned that you 
will be getting visibility from the innovator for the large contract for volume visibility. I 
wanted to ask whether it will be just for the next few months or it will be for the entire 
five-year duration? 
Deepak Jain: 
We will let you know, Harsh. I cannot answer that question right now because like I 
said, there are multiple scenarios possible here. We have narrowed down on certain 
scenarios, we are discussing the pros and cons. We will we will let you know soon. 
Harsh Shah: 
All right. So, my next question is you have been in your earlier conversation you have 
said that FY27 to be a solid year. You are saying solid revenue growth. So, and also 
you have said that you will reach peak utilization of all our assets by end of FY27. Do 
you still maintain that outlook? 
Deepak Jain: 
Yes, so I think I probably did not say the peak, but yes, what is true is whatever 
investments we made in the last three, three and a half years, a lot of them will start 
reaching average 70% plus utilization levels by end of this fiscal year. And hence, we 
to the earlier question on capex, we need to keep creating new plants, which is what 
we are doing to enable our incremental growth from here. 
Harsh Shah: 
So, my final question would be the 100 plus molecule pipeline that you that we have 
been talking about. When can we expect the ramp up or the conversion in the rest of 
the pipeline? 
Deepak Jain: 
See, the conversion is happening as we move. Every quarter, we get confirmation on 
at least a few more molecules from that and at the same time, of course, some 
molecules drop from the pipeline as well, as you can imagine, it is a dynamic 
pipeline, but like I said in response to an earlier question, even without taking the big 
contract into account, the rest of the confirmed pipeline where we already have some 
commercial confirmations, the peak revenue of that is INR1,500 crore and at least 
one third of that will happen this year itself. 
And we hope to scale it up from here in the coming two years. At the same time, 
those 25 plus molecules should also expand because from the 100 plus pipeline that 

 
Page 10 of 12 
 
we talked about in the previous quarters, if you see in last four quarters itself, we 
have confirmed at least 25 plus molecules. So, if you just take that average, you can 
extrapolate and see how our confirmed molecule pipeline is moving. 
Harsh Shah: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you. Next question is from the line of Ravi Mehta from OneUp Financial. 
Please go ahead. 
Ravi Mehta: 
Yes, thanks for taking my call. Just one question. You mentioned that these specialty 
chemicals can grow, even the EBITDA can grow at 20%, 25%, the way you are 
adding the molecules and the pipeline converting. I just wanted to check, when we 
look at the H1 EBITDA, it has grown 10%. So is it that the large order that we are 
executing, the EBITDA is back-ended, or how should we look at this H1 EBITDA 
growth? 
Deepak Jain: 
No, Ravi, see, what I said is 20%, 25% as a multi-year average. I think you should 
look at our specialty chemical business, by the way, together with nutrition because 
we treat them together, and look at the last three years, how our EBITDA has more 
than doubled in the last three years. So that, that is more than 25% EBITDA growth 
in that portfolio. 
We, with all the pipeline we have and investments we are making, we are reasonably 
confident that we will be able to maintain that as a multi-year growth. But at the same 
time, because some, some of these projects are lumpy in nature, right, you start and 
then start constructing the plant and the revenue start coming after some lag, you 
should not look at one quarter or just one half of the year. 
To measure the real growth rate. Look at it as a multi-year trajectory and that will give 
you the answer or clarity on how the growth rate has been on the specialty as well as 
nutrition if you put together both of them, which is almost, I think, doubled in the last 
three years. 
Ravi Mehta: 
Okay. And another question was on the revenue addition. So when you say X of 
large order, the peak pipeline line has a revenue attribution of INR1,500 crore and 
INR500 crore can flow through this year. When I see again the H1 numbers, there is 
a delta of INR300 crore in the Spec-Chem, and that includes a large order which is 
being executed. So is this bulk of INR500 crore going to happen in the next two 
quarters? 
Deepak Jain: 
See, I think of course part of it will come in the subsequent two quarters as well. So 
you should do that calculation again at the end of the year. Number 2, of course, as 
we expand this, there are of course some, let us say, current products also were, 
which might not have kicked in the first two quarters. 
And hence, you see, you see some uplift coming from new products while existing 
products, let us say, not having deliveries scheduled in the first two quarters. So 
there are multiple factors playing out there. So it is not a, not a straight math that you 
just add revenue of new molecules on the back of last year revenue and you get to 
this year revenue. There are multiple factors. Of course, there is pricing also playing 
a bigger part here. 

 
Page 11 of 12 
 
So all the combined factor or combined effect of all of that is what you should look at, 
which will give you a good sense of how our portfolio is moving. 
Ravi Mehta: 
Sure. And on the pricing part only, is there any segment of revenue where we see 
there is a pressure on the pricing and there is a rundown effect on the base? So 
when keep adding the new contracts and revenues, we also have to be mindful of 
some rundown of the base? 
Deepak Jain: 
That is exactly what I meant, right? That is exactly what I meant, that obviously there 
are some segments, as I said in my opening remarks also, there is some pricing 
pressure on base pyridine, there is some pricing pressure coming for B3, which are 
the normal factors which play out in our portfolio every year. 
If you see for last three years or five years. Q3, generally pricing goes down now in 
coming the current quarter for vitamin B3. So all those factors are playing out, and 
hence my comment that it is a very dynamic portfolio with so many forces acting on 
it, on old products, new products, on the volume side, and of course on the pricing 
side also. Like you said, there was, there was a tailwind on many products in terms of 
increased pricing, but at the same time like you said, there is rundown on couple of 
product portfolios. So what you see on the overall portfolio is the combined effect of 
everything. 
Ravi Mehta: 
Okay, so we do not expect any further rundown or pressure? It is already there in the 
numbers what we are seeing? 
Deepak Jain:
